svg.aria-label: Hole-by-hole breadboard map for Pico 2 W, OLED, IR LED and button
svg.text: Column 1 on the left (numbers printed on the board). USB hangs off that end, chip facing you. Unplug USB while inserting parts.
Blue holes = Pico pins. Yellow = a jumper or component lead. Red hole e1 = 5 V, leave empty. GP16–GP19 are on the top row.
centre trench — insulator. Pico bridges it like a DIP chip.
row e = Pico pins 40 … 21 (VBUS at USB, GP16 at antenna)
row f = Pico pins 1 … 20 (GP0 at USB)
typical Pi Hut order — if labels differ, keep a23–a26 and move the four wires
Push the Pico across the trench, USB off the left, chip
facing you. 20 pins in row e, 20 pins in row f.
e1 = pin 40 VBUS (empty) f1 = pin 1 GP0
e17 = pin 24 GP18 e16 = pin 25 GP19
e19 = pin 22 GP17 e20 = pin 21 GP16
Short jumpers above the Pico, then join the long rails:
black bottom GND col 34 → top GND col 34
Leave e1 empty. That pin is 5 V from USB.
a–e in column 17 are already joined to Pico GP18.
a–e in column 16 are already joined to Pico GP19.
a–e in column 19 / 20 are GP17 / GP16.
Columns 37–63 of a full-size board stay empty.
2. OLED — pins in a23 a24 a25 a26
Four pins in row a. Screen hangs off the top of the board.
GND a24 → top GND rail (short black)
These stay on the top side. They do not cross the trench.
Long lead (anode) in c32. Short lead / flat rim in c33.
Before you plug USB back in
• Pico straddles the trench, USB on the left
• e1 is empty (no 5 V on the rails)
• OLED VCC comes from +3V3, not VBUS
• LED resistor is 220 Ω, never 15 Ω
• Long LED lead is in c32 (anode)
• Point the LED at the other board’s TSOP
Power is the Pico USB cable. No battery.
Later player boards drive the LED with a transistor on GP0.
